source.text: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ;

records.literal_gloss: I say then, not did reject the God the people of him?

en.L: I say then, did God reject {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people?
en.B: So I ask: has God rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people?
en.R: So I ask this: Has God rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people?

es.L: Digo, pues: ¿acaso rechazó Dios a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo?
es.B: Pregunto, entonces: ¿ha rechazado Dios a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo?
es.R: Entonces pregunto: ¿Ha rechazado Dios a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio pueblo?

sw.L: Basi nasema, je, Mungu aliwakataa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}?
sw.B: Basi nauliza: Je, Mungu amewakataa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nauliza hivi: Je, Mungu amewakataa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}?

fr.L: Je dis donc : Dieu aurait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rejeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple ?
fr.B: Je pose donc la question : Dieu aurait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rejeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple ?
fr.R: Alors je pose cette question : Dieu aurait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rejeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre peuple ?

ko.L: 그러면 내가 말합니다. 하나님께서 그분의 백성을 버리셨습니까?
ko.B: 그러면 내가 묻겠습니다. 하나님께서 그분의 백성을 버리셨다는 말입니까?
ko.R: 그러면 이렇게 묻겠습니다. 하나님께서 그분의 백성을 버리셨다는 말입니까?

vi.L: Vậy tôi nói: chẳng lẽ Đức Chúa Trời đã ruồng bỏ dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sao?
vi.B: Vậy tôi hỏi: Đức Chúa Trời đã ruồng bỏ dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rồi sao?
vi.R: Vậy tôi hỏi điều này: Đức Chúa Trời đã ruồng bỏ chính dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rồi sao?

pt.L: Digo, então: Deus rejeitou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo?
pt.B: Então eu pergunto: Deus rejeitou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo?
pt.R: Então eu pergunto: Deus rejeitou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} próprio povo?

am.L: እንግዲህ እላለሁ፣ እግዚአብሔር ሕዝቡን ጣለ [ይሆን]?
am.B: እንግዲህ እጠይቃለሁ፤ እግዚአብሔር ሕዝቡን ጥሏልን?
am.R: ስለዚህ ይህን እጠይቃለሁ፤ እግዚአብሔር የራሱን ሕዝብ ጥሏልን?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The question begins with a negative particle that expects a denial, and Paul gives one at once: "May it not be!"

decisions.choice: Psalm 94:14 and 1 Samuel 12:22
decisions.reason: The words echo the promise that God will not reject his people (Psalm 94:14; 1 Samuel 12:22). The Hebrew of both verses has the divine name. Verse 2 turns the question into the answer: "God did not reject his people."

decisions.choice: his people: Israel as the people God chose for himself
decisions.reason: After chapters 9-10, the question is whether Israel's unbelief means God has cast off the nation he chose.

decisions.choice: I ask
decisions.reason: The verb is "I say", but it introduces a question, so Balanced and Readable say "I ask".

decisions.choice: spans only on free pronouns and possessives ("watu wake")
alternatives: a span for every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: As in Romans 1:1, Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("aliwakataa", "aliwajua"), where a capital is impossible, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, and this chapter has fewer spans than the English.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God carries the span wherever the English "he" does, also in a question ("Dieu aurait-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rejeté"), and where French needs a pronoun the English lacks. When God speaks or is spoken to in the quotations, "me", "moi", "ma", "mon" and "tes" carry it; "je" does not. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: the conditional "aurait-il rejeté" for a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The Greek question expects "no" (meaning decision). French says that with the conditional, which voices a suggestion the speaker is about to reject; a plain "a-t-il rejeté ?" would sound like a real question. The same form is used in 11:11 and in 10:18-19.

decisions.choice: 합쇼체 with "여러분" continues; "내가 묻겠습니다" (B, R) and "... 말입니까?" for a question expecting "no", as in 10:18-19; no deity_pronoun spans (as through the letter)
decisions.reason: As settled at 1:1 and 10:18. Korean has no capital letters for the deity_pronoun setting to change; respect for God is carried by -시- and 께서.

decisions.choice: "ruồng bỏ" at every level (also 11:2)
decisions.reason: The verb is to push away, to reject (m1). "Ruồng bỏ" is to cast off someone who belongs to you, which suits God and his own people; "loại bỏ" is kept for a different word in 11:15.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Christ has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns (እርሱ, እኔ, the verb endings) are written once, with no span.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ Ἰσραηλίτης εἰμί, ἐκ σπέρματος Ἀβραάμ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν.

records.literal_gloss: Not may it be; also for I an Israelite am, from seed of Abraham, of tribe of Benjamin.

en.L: May it not be! For I also am an Israelite, from [the] seed of Abraham, of [the] tribe of Benjamin.
en.B: Certainly not! I myself am an Israelite, descended from Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
en.R: Of course not! I am an Israelite too. I come from Abraham's family, from the tribe of Benjamin.

es.L: ¡No sea así! Porque también yo soy israelita, de [la] descendencia de Abraham, de [la] tribu de Benjamín.
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Yo mismo soy israelita, descendiente de Abraham, de la tribu de Benjamín.
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Yo también soy israelita. Vengo de la familia de Abraham, de la tribu de Benjamín.

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Kwa maana mimi pia ni Mwisraeli, wa uzao wa Abrahamu, wa kabila la Benyamini.
sw.B: Hasha! Mimi mwenyewe ni Mwisraeli, mzao wa Abrahamu, wa kabila la Benyamini.
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Mimi pia ni Mwisraeli. Ninatoka katika ukoo wa Abrahamu, katika kabila la Benyamini.

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Car moi aussi je suis Israélite, de [la] descendance d’Abraham, de [la] tribu de Benjamin.
fr.B: Absolument pas ! Je suis moi-même Israélite, descendant d’Abraham, de la tribu de Benjamin.
fr.R: Pas du tout ! Moi aussi, je suis Israélite. Je viens de la famille d’Abraham, de la tribu de Benjamin.

ko.L: 결코 그럴 수 없습니다! 나도 이스라엘 사람이요, 아브라함의 씨에서 [났고], 베냐민 지파 [사람]이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 절대로 그렇지 않습니다! 나 자신도 이스라엘 사람이며, 아브라함의 후손이고, 베냐민 지파에 속한 사람입니다.
ko.R: 절대 아닙니다! 나도 이스라엘 사람입니다. 나는 아브라함의 자손이고, 베냐민 지파 사람입니다.

vi.L: Không hề như vậy! Vì chính tôi cũng là người Y-sơ-ra-ên, từ dòng dõi Áp-ra-ham, thuộc chi phái Bên-gia-min.
vi.B: Chẳng hề như vậy! Chính tôi cũng là người Y-sơ-ra-ên, thuộc dòng dõi Áp-ra-ham, chi phái Bên-gia-min.
vi.R: Không đời nào! Tôi cũng là người Y-sơ-ra-ên. Tôi thuộc dòng con cháu Áp-ra-ham, chi phái Bên-gia-min.

pt.L: Que não aconteça! Pois também eu sou israelita, da descendência de Abraão, da tribo de Benjamim.
pt.B: De forma alguma! Eu mesmo sou israelita, descendente de Abraão, da tribo de Benjamim.
pt.R: Claro que não! Eu também sou israelita. Venho da família de Abraão, da tribo de Benjamim.

am.L: ከቶ አይሁን! እኔም ደግሞ ከአብርሃም ዘር፣ ከብንያም ነገድ የሆንኩ እስራኤላዊ ነኝና።
am.B: በፍጹም! እኔ ራሴ የአብርሃም ዘር፣ ከብንያም ነገድ የሆንኩ እስራኤላዊ ነኝ።
am.R: በጭራሽ! እኔም እስራኤላዊ ነኝ። የአብርሃም ቤተሰብ ነኝ፤ ከብንያም ነገድ ነኝ።

decisions.choice: the strongest possible denial
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο, "may it not happen", is Paul's strongest way of rejecting a false conclusion (3:4, 6:2, 9:14; Galatians 2:17).

decisions.choice: Paul himself is proof that God has not rejected Israel
alternatives: Paul, as an Israelite, could not believe that God would reject his own people
decisions.reason: Paul is a Jew who believes in Jesus, so God has plainly not cast off every Israelite. Verses 2-5 go on to speak of the faithful few in Elijah's day and a remnant now, which fits this reading.

decisions.choice: descended from Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin
decisions.reason: Paul names his descent as he does in Philippians 3:5 and 2 Corinthians 11:22. Benjamin was the tribe of King Saul, whose name Paul also bore.

decisions.choice: descended from Abraham (B); from Abraham's family (R)
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring; Balanced and Readable use plain words for it.

decisions.choice: Certainly not! (B); Of course not! (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use ordinary English for an emphatic no. "God forbid" adds a word for God that the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: ¡No sea así! (L); ¡De ningún modo! (B); ¡Claro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of a wish, "let it not be so"; Balanced and Readable use ordinary emphatic Spanish. "¡Dios nos libre!" would add a word for God that the Greek does not have. The same wording serves for this phrase in verse 11.

decisions.choice: Isiwe hivyo! (L); Hasha! (B); Sivyo kabisa! (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of a wish, "let it not be so"; "Hasha!" is the standard emphatic Swahili no, and Readable says "not at all". "Mungu apishe mbali" would add a word for God that the Greek does not have. The same wording serves for this phrase in verse 11.

decisions.choice: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! (L); Absolument pas ! (B); Pas du tout ! (R), as in 9:14 (also 11:11)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a wish, "may it not be", used as the strongest possible denial. Literal keeps the form of a wish with a French expression that still lives; Balanced and Readable say the denial as French says it.

decisions.choice: "결코 그럴 수 없습니다!" (L); "절대로 그렇지 않습니다!" (B); "절대 아닙니다!" (R), as settled at 3:4
decisions.reason: The same fixed form for each level as through the letter.

decisions.choice: "씨" (L); "후손" (B); "자손" (R), as settled at 4:13
decisions.reason: The letter's fixed rendering of "seed" for each level.

decisions.choice: "Bên-gia-min", "Ê-li", "Ba-anh", "Đa-vít", "Si-ôn", "Gia-cốp" (this chapter); "chi phái" for tribe
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliterations the style guide sets for names. "Chi phái" is the established word for one of the tribes of Israel.

decisions.choice: ከቶ አይሁን! (L); በፍጹም! (B); በጭራሽ! (R)
decisions.reason: Paul's strongest denial, rendered as in Romans 6 and 7 so the formula reads the same through the letter: Literal keeps the wish form, Balanced and Readable say an emphatic 'never'.

source.text: οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ὃν προέγνω.

records.literal_gloss: Not did reject the God the people of him whom he foreknew.

en.L: God did not reject {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} foreknew.
en.B: God has not rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} foreknew.
en.R: No, God has not rejected {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He knew them and chose them from the beginning.

es.L: No rechazó Dios a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, al cual conoció de antemano.
es.B: Dios no ha rechazado a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo, al que de antemano conoció.
es.R: No, Dios no ha rechazado a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo. Desde el principio lo conoció y lo eligió.

sw.L: Mungu hakuwakataa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} aliowajua kabla.
sw.B: Mungu hajawakataa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, aliowajua tangu awali.
sw.R: Hapana, Mungu hajawakataa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Aliwajua na kuwachagua tangu mwanzo.

fr.L: Dieu n’a pas rejeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a connu d’avance.
fr.B: Dieu n’a pas rejeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple, ce peuple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a connu d’avance.
fr.R: Non, Dieu n’a pas rejeté {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple. Il a connu ce peuple et l’a choisi dès le commencement.

ko.L: 하나님께서는 미리 아신 그분의 백성을 버리지 않으셨습니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 미리 아신 그분의 백성을 버리지 않으셨습니다.
ko.R: 아닙니다. 하나님께서는 그분의 백성을 버리지 않으셨습니다. 하나님께서는 처음부터 그들을 아시고 그분의 백성으로 택하셨습니다.

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời đã không ruồng bỏ dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã biết trước.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời đã không ruồng bỏ dân mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã biết trước.
vi.R: Không, Đức Chúa Trời không ruồng bỏ dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài đã biết và chọn họ từ ban đầu.

pt.L: Deus não rejeitou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo, que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} conheceu de antemão.
pt.B: Deus não rejeitou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo, que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} conheceu de antemão.
pt.R: Não, Deus não rejeitou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} povo. Desde o princípio {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} o conhecia e o escolheu.

am.L: እግዚአብሔር አስቀድሞ ያወቀውን ሕዝቡን አልጣለም።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር አስቀድሞ ያወቀውን ሕዝቡን አልጣለውም።
am.R: አይደለም፤ እግዚአብሔር ሕዝቡን አልጣለም። ገና ከመጀመሪያው አውቋቸዋል፤ መርጧቸዋልም።

decisions.choice: foreknew: knew beforehand in the sense of choosing them as his own
alternatives: knew in advance what they would do
decisions.reason: In Scripture God's "knowing" a people often means choosing them in love (Amos 3:2), and in 8:29 the same verb stands beside "predestined". Israel was chosen before it did anything (9:11).

decisions.choice: "whom he foreknew" describes the whole people
alternatives: it marks out a part of the people: those of Israel whom he foreknew
decisions.reason: Verse 1 asks about God's people as a whole, and the answer repeats its words. The clause gives the reason God will not reject them: he chose them. Verses 5-7 then speak of a remnant within the people.

decisions.choice: He knew them and chose them from the beginning
decisions.reason: Readable explains "foreknew" as the meaning decision describes it.

decisions.choice: "미리 알다" (L, B); "처음부터 ... 아시고 ... 택하셨다" (R), as at 8:29
decisions.reason: Foreknew means knew beforehand in the sense of choosing them as his own (meaning decision); Readable says both, as at 8:29.

decisions.choice: "biết trước" (L, B), as in 8:29
decisions.reason: Foreknew is knowing beforehand in the sense of choosing them as his own (m1), the verb of 8:29, so the same words are kept; Readable spells out the choosing, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: conheceu de antemão
decisions.reason: "Conhecer de antemão" keeps the verb "know", which the meaning decision reads as choosing in love; "prever" would say only that God saw it in advance.

source.text: ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή, ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰσραήλ;

records.literal_gloss: Or not you know in Elijah what says the Scripture, how he pleads with the God against the Israel?

en.L: Or do you not know what the Scripture says in [the passage about] Elijah, how he pleads with God against Israel?
en.B: Or do you not know what Scripture says in the story of Elijah, how he appealed to God against Israel?
en.R: Do you remember what Scripture says in the story of Elijah? He complained to God about the people of Israel.

es.L: ¿O no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que dice la Escritura en [el pasaje de] Elías, cómo apela a Dios contra Israel?
es.B: ¿O no {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} lo que dice la Escritura en la historia de Elías, cómo apeló a Dios contra Israel?
es.R: ¿{{plural_you:Recuerdan|Recordáis}} lo que dice la Escritura en la historia de Elías? Se quejó ante Dios contra el pueblo de Israel.

sw.L: Au hamjui Maandiko yanavyosema katika [habari za] Eliya, jinsi anavyomsihi Mungu dhidi ya Israeli?
sw.B: Au hamjui Maandiko yanavyosema katika habari za Eliya, jinsi alivyomlalamikia Mungu kuhusu Israeli?
sw.R: Je, mnakumbuka Maandiko yanavyosema katika habari za Eliya? Alimlalamikia Mungu juu ya watu wa Israeli.

fr.L: Ou ne savez-vous pas ce que dit l’Écriture dans [le passage sur] Élie, comment il en appelle à Dieu contre Israël ?
fr.B: Ne savez-vous pas ce que dit l’Écriture dans l’histoire d’Élie, quand il en a appelé à Dieu contre Israël ?
fr.R: Vous souvenez-vous de ce que dit l’Écriture dans l’histoire d’Élie ? Il s’est plaint à Dieu du peuple d’Israël.

ko.L: 아니면 여러분은 엘리야 [이야기]에서 성경이 무엇이라고 말하는지, 그가 어떻게 하나님께 이스라엘을 고발하며 호소하는지 알지 못합니까?
ko.B: 아니면 여러분은 엘리야 이야기에서 성경이 무엇이라고 말하는지 모릅니까? 엘리야는 하나님께 이스라엘을 고발하며 이렇게 호소했습니다.
ko.R: 성경의 엘리야 이야기를 기억합니까? 엘리야는 하나님께 이스라엘 백성에 대해 이렇게 불평했습니다.

vi.L: Hay anh chị em không biết Kinh Thánh nói gì trong [đoạn về] Ê-li, thể nào ông kêu xin với Đức Chúa Trời chống lại Y-sơ-ra-ên sao?
vi.B: Hay anh chị em không biết Kinh Thánh nói gì trong câu chuyện về Ê-li, khi ông tố cáo Y-sơ-ra-ên trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời?
vi.R: Anh chị em có nhớ Kinh Thánh nói gì trong câu chuyện về Ê-li không? Ông đã than phiền với Đức Chúa Trời về dân Y-sơ-ra-ên.

pt.L: Ou vocês não sabem o que a Escritura diz em [a passagem sobre] Elias, como ele apela a Deus contra Israel?

decisions.choice: in Elijah: in the passage that tells about Elijah
decisions.reason: Before chapters and verses existed, a passage was named by its subject, as Mark 12:26 says "at the bush" for the story of Moses at the burning bush. The story is 1 Kings 19.

decisions.choice: he appealed to God against Israel: he accused Israel before God
alternatives: he prayed to God for Israel
decisions.reason: The verb means to approach someone with a request; with "against" it means to bring a complaint. Elijah's words in verse 3 are an accusation.

decisions.choice: in the story of Elijah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "in Elijah" refers to.

decisions.choice: appealed (B); complained (R)
decisions.reason: The present tense of the Greek tells a past story vividly; English tells it in the past. "Intercedes" would suggest prayer on Israel's behalf.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} (ustedes / vosotros forms)
decisions.reason: As throughout Romans (1:1), every plural "you" addressed to the readers is a reader setting: ustedes forms by default, vosotros forms as the alternative. Verses 17-24 speak to one imagined reader as "tú", which is not a setting.

decisions.choice: "고발하며 호소하다" (L, B); "불평하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the Spirit's and Christ's pleading in 8:26-34 ("간구하다"), but here it is "against Israel": Elijah accuses Israel before God (meaning decision), so Korean says "고발하며 호소하다".

decisions.choice: "kêu xin ... chống lại" (L); "tố cáo ... trước mặt" (B); "than phiền" (R)
decisions.reason: This is the verb kept as "cầu thay" (to plead for) in 8:26 and 8:34, but here Elijah pleads against Israel, accusing them before God (m2), so "cầu thay" cannot be used. Literal keeps the pleading, Balanced says what it is.

decisions.choice: recorreu a Deus contra Israel
decisions.reason: "Recorrer a alguém contra" is the Portuguese for taking a complaint to an authority, which is what the meaning decision describes; "interceder" would suggest prayer on Israel's behalf.

decisions.choice: ከሰሰ (accused, B); አቤቱታ አቀረበ (complained, R)
decisions.reason: In Amharic church use ማለደ means to plead on someone's behalf, the opposite of what Elijah did; the meaning note says he accused Israel before God. Literal uses the neutral ያመለክታል, 'petitions'.

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 19:10 and 19:14
decisions.reason: Paul quotes Elijah's complaint in shortened form, putting the prophets before the altars and adding the address "Lord". In the Hebrew, Elijah speaks of the divine name just before: he has been zealous for the LORD, the God of hosts.

decisions.choice: they are seeking my life: they are trying to kill me
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" is a Hebrew way of saying "try to kill"; Jezebel had sworn to kill Elijah (1 Kings 19:2).

decisions.choice: trying to take my life (B); want to kill me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom.

decisions.choice: Elijah speaks to God in 합쇼체 with "주님" and the humble "저/제"
decisions.reason: Words addressed to God take 합쇼체, as at 10:16; one who prays speaks of himself with "저", as the Korean style guide sets for the psalms. "주님" with no divine_name span: the Greek has kyrios.

decisions.choice: "Lạy Chúa", "Ngài" for God and "tôi" for Elijah
decisions.reason: As in 8:36, the one who prays in an Old Testament quotation says "tôi" and speaks to God as "Ngài", as the style guide sets for the psalmist.

decisions.choice: tu (teus profetas, teus altares)
decisions.reason: Elijah speaks to God, so he says "tu" at every level, as in all prayer in this translation.

decisions.choice: 1 Kings 19:18
decisions.reason: Paul gives God's answer freely. The Hebrew says "I will leave seven thousand in Israel"; Paul adds "for myself", stressing that God himself kept them faithful. In the Hebrew the answer is given by the LORD (the divine name, 1 Kings 19:15).

decisions.choice: people: the faithful Israelites, counted by heads
decisions.reason: The Greek word normally means men, but the Hebrew of 1 Kings 19:18 has no word for men, and Paul's point is the faithful remnant of Israel, not its males.

decisions.choice: bending the knee: worshiping
decisions.reason: Kneeling before a god was the act of worship (Isaiah 45:23). Baal was the Canaanite storm god whose worship Ahab and Jezebel promoted. The Greek puts a feminine article before the name (τῇ Βάαλ), as the old Greek translation sometimes does; this may reflect the Jewish custom of reading "shame" in place of the god's name.

decisions.choice: bowed down to worship
decisions.reason: Readable explains the gesture.

decisions.choice: watu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Watu" means people of either sex, which is the sense the meaning decision gives. "Wanaume" means males and would change the meaning, so Swahili has no counterpart to the English gender span. "For myself" is inside the verb ("Nimejibakizia", "Nimejiwekea") and takes no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: "칠천 명" (L, R); "사람 칠천 명" (B), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek counts "men", but the meaning decision says they are the faithful Israelites counted by heads. Korean counts people with "명", which says nothing about sex, so no setting is needed; God speaks in 해라체 with "나", as settled at 9:7.

decisions.choice: "bảy nghìn người", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as people counted by heads, with a footnote for men. Vietnamese "người" already counts persons without marking sex, as elsewhere in the Vietnamese Romans (2:1), so the English gender span is not copied.

decisions.choice: one sentence
alternatives: Guardei ... sete mil pessoas. Elas não se ajoelharam ...
decisions.reason: The English Readable splits the verse, but a Portuguese pronoun starting the second sentence would have to agree with "pessoas" or "homens" and could not follow the gender setting; Readable keeps the relative clause, which reads plainly under both options.

decisions.choice: ሰዎች (people), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Amharic ሰዎች already counts people of both sexes, which is the sense of the meaning note; there is no second wording for the setting to switch to. This holds for the chapter.

sw.L: Basi hivyo hivyo pia katika wakati wa sasa yamekuwepo mabaki kwa kadiri ya uchaguzi wa neema.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo, hata wakati huu wa sasa kuna mabaki, yaliyochaguliwa kwa neema.
sw.R: Ndivyo ilivyo leo pia. Bado wapo baadhi ya Waisraeli waliosalia, mabaki ambayo Mungu ameyachagua kwa neema {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

fr.L: Ainsi donc, dans le temps présent aussi, il existe un reste selon [l’]élection de [la] grâce.
fr.B: De même, aujourd’hui encore, il y a un reste, choisi par grâce.
fr.R: C’est la même chose aujourd’hui. Il reste encore une partie d’Israël, un reste que Dieu a choisi par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} grâce.

ko.L: 그러므로 이와 같이 지금 이때에도 은혜의 택하심을 따라 남은 자가 생겼습니다.
ko.B: 이와 같이 지금 이때에도 은혜로 택하심을 받은 남은 사람들이 있습니다.
ko.R: 오늘날도 마찬가지입니다. 이스라엘 가운데 아직 남아 있는 사람들이 있습니다. 하나님께서 그분의 은혜로 그들을 택하셨습니다.

vi.L: Vậy cũng thế, trong thời hiện tại có một phần sót lại theo sự lựa chọn của ân điển.
vi.B: Cũng vậy, ngày nay vẫn có một phần dân sót lại được chọn bởi ân điển.
vi.R: Ngày nay cũng thế. Vẫn còn một số người Y-sơ-ra-ên, là phần dân sót lại mà Đức Chúa Trời đã chọn bởi ân điển của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: Assim, pois, também no tempo presente veio a haver um remanescente segundo [a] eleição da graça.
pt.B: Do mesmo modo, também no tempo presente há um remanescente, escolhido pela graça.
pt.R: Hoje acontece a mesma coisa. Ainda restam alguns do povo de Israel, um remanescente que Deus escolheu pela {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} graça.

am.L: እንግዲህ እንዲሁ ደግሞ በአሁኑ ዘመን በጸጋ ምርጫ መሠረት ቅሬታ ተገኝቷል።
am.B: እንዲሁም በአሁኑ ጊዜ በጸጋ የተመረጠ ቅሬታ አለ።
am.R: ዛሬም እንዲሁ ነው። ከእስራኤል ጥቂቶች አሁንም ቀርተዋል፤ እነርሱም እግዚአብሔር በጸጋው የመረጣቸው ናቸው።

decisions.choice: remnant: the part of Israel that God keeps for himself
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of a remnant of Israel that would survive judgment and return to God (Isaiah 10:20-22, quoted in 9:27). The seven thousand of Elijah's day were such a remnant; the Jews who now believe in Jesus are another.

decisions.choice: chosen by grace: a choice that comes from God's grace
alternatives: a choice that consists in grace
decisions.reason: "Election of grace" means God's choosing, which springs from grace and not from anything in the people chosen, as verse 6 explains.

decisions.choice: Some of Israel are still left, a remnant
decisions.reason: Readable says what a remnant is before using the word.

decisions.choice: mabaki
decisions.reason: "Mabaki" is the everyday word for what is left over, and it carries the prophets' picture of a part of Israel that remains. Readable first says "waliosalia" (those who are left), as the English Readable explains the word before using it.

decisions.choice: l’élection (L); choisi (B, R), as in 9:11 (also 11:7 and 11:28)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "élection", the theological word for God’s choosing, so the term can be followed through these chapters. In everyday French "élection" means a vote, so Balanced and Readable say "choisir" and "choix".

decisions.choice: "남은 자" (L); "남은 사람들" (B, R), as at 9:27; "택하심" for God's choosing
decisions.reason: The same words as at 9:27 and 9:11, so the remnant here is linked to the remnant of Isaiah's prophecy.

decisions.choice: "phần sót lại" (L), "phần dân sót lại" (B, R), as in 9:27; "sự lựa chọn" (L) for election (also 11:7, 11:28)
decisions.reason: The remnant is the part of Israel God keeps for himself (m1), the word of 9:27. Election is God's choosing (m2); "sự lựa chọn" is plain and keeps the verb "chọn" that Balanced and Readable use.

decisions.choice: um remanescente
decisions.reason: "Remanescente" is the Portuguese word for the remnant of the prophets; "resto" is ordinary but can sound like leftovers. Readable first says what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ቅሬታ (remnant)
alternatives: የቀሩ ጥቂቶች (a few who are left)
decisions.reason: ቅሬታ is the Bible's word for the remnant God keeps; because in everyday Amharic it also means a grievance, Readable says plainly "ጥቂቶች ... ቀርተዋል".

source.text: εἰ δὲ χάριτι, οὐκέτι ἐξ ἔργων, ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις οὐκέτι γίνεται χάρις.

records.literal_gloss: If and by grace, no longer from works, since the grace no longer becomes grace.

en.L: And if by grace, [it is] no longer from works, since [then] grace would no longer be grace.
en.B: And if it is by grace, it does not come from works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.
en.R: And if God chose them by grace, then it was not because of what they did. If it were, grace would not really be grace.

es.L: Y si [es] por gracia, ya no [es] por obras, pues [de otro modo] la gracia ya no sería gracia.
es.B: Y si es por gracia, no proviene de las obras; si así fuera, la gracia dejaría de ser gracia.
es.R: Y si Dios los eligió por gracia, entonces no fue por lo que ellos hicieron. Si fuera así, la gracia no sería realmente gracia.

sw.L: Na ikiwa ni kwa neema, si kwa matendo tena, kwa maana [vinginevyo] neema isingekuwa neema tena.
sw.B: Na ikiwa ni kwa neema, basi haitokani tena na matendo; vinginevyo neema ingekoma kuwa neema.
sw.R: Na kama Mungu aliwachagua kwa neema, basi haikuwa kwa sababu ya mambo waliyoyafanya. Kama ingekuwa hivyo, neema isingekuwa neema kweli.

fr.L: Or si [c’est] par grâce, [ce n’est] plus par les œuvres, puisque [autrement] la grâce ne serait plus grâce.
fr.B: Et si c’est par grâce, ce n’est pas par les œuvres ; sinon la grâce ne serait plus la grâce.
fr.R: Et si Dieu les a choisis par grâce, ce n’est pas à cause de ce qu’ils ont fait. Sinon, la grâce ne serait plus vraiment la grâce.

ko.L: 그런데 은혜로 [된 것]이면, 더 이상 행위에서 [난 것이] 아닙니다. 그렇지 않으면 은혜가 더 이상 은혜가 되지 못합니다.
ko.B: 은혜로 된 것이라면, 더 이상 행위로 된 것이 아닙니다. 그렇지 않다면 은혜는 더 이상 은혜가 아닐 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 은혜로 그들을 택하셨다면, 그것은 그들이 한 일 때문이 아닙니다. 만일 그들이 한 일 때문이라면, 은혜는 참된 은혜가 아닐 것입니다.

vi.L: Mà nếu bởi ân điển, thì không còn bởi việc làm nữa, vì [nếu không thì] ân điển không còn là ân điển nữa.
vi.B: Mà nếu là bởi ân điển, thì không phải bởi việc làm; bằng không, ân điển sẽ không còn là ân điển nữa.
vi.R: Nếu Đức Chúa Trời chọn họ bởi ân điển, thì không phải vì những việc họ đã làm. Nếu vì việc làm, ân điển sẽ không còn thật là ân điển.

pt.L: E, se [é] pela graça, já não [é] pelas obras; do contrário, a graça já não seria graça.
pt.B: E, se é pela graça, não vem das obras; do contrário, a graça já não seria graça.
pt.R: E, se Deus os escolheu pela graça, não foi por causa do que eles fizeram. Se fosse, a graça não seria graça de verdade.

am.L: በጸጋ ከሆነ ግን ከእንግዲህ ከሥራ አይደለም፤ ያለዚያ ጸጋ ከእንግዲህ ጸጋ አይሆንምና።
am.B: በጸጋ ከሆነ ደግሞ ከሥራ የተነሣ አይደለም፤ አለበለዚያ ጸጋ ጸጋ መሆኑ ይቀራል።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር በጸጋ ከመረጣቸው ደግሞ ባደረጉት ነገር ምክንያት አይደለም። እንደዚያ ቢሆን ኖሮ ጸጋ በእርግጥ ጸጋ ባልሆነ ነበር።

decisions.choice: if it is by grace: if the remnant is chosen by grace
decisions.reason: The sentence leaves out its subject; it continues verse 5, where the remnant is chosen by grace.

decisions.choice: works: anything people do to earn God's choice
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Romans "works" are often the works the law requires (3:20, 3:28), but here they stand against grace in general, as in 4:4-5 and 9:11-12.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends with "grace would no longer be grace"
alternatives: some later manuscripts add: "But if it is by works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work"
decisions.reason: The longer text is found in later manuscripts and in the King James Version; the oldest manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers must check the details against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: what they did
decisions.reason: Readable says what "works" means, as elsewhere in Romans and Galatians.

decisions.choice: "행위" (L, B); "그들이 한 일" (R)
decisions.reason: Works are anything people do to earn God's choice (meaning decision); "행위" is the letter's word (3:20, 9:32); Readable uses the plain phrase.

source.text: τί οὖν;

records.literal_gloss: What then?

en.L: What then?
en.B: What then?
en.R: So what does this mean?

es.L: ¿Qué, pues?
es.B: ¿Qué, entonces?
es.R: Entonces, ¿qué significa esto?

sw.L: Basi nini?
sw.B: Basi je?
sw.R: Basi, hii ina maana gani?

fr.L: Quoi donc ?
fr.B: Quoi donc ?
fr.R: Alors, qu’est-ce que cela veut dire ?

ko.L: 그러면 무엇입니까?
ko.B: 그러면 어떻게 된 것입니까?
ko.R: 그렇다면 이것은 무슨 뜻입니까?

vi.L: Vậy thì sao?
vi.B: Vậy thì sao?
vi.R: Vậy điều này có nghĩa là gì?

pt.L: Que, pois?
pt.B: E então?
pt.R: Então, o que isso quer dizer?

am.L: እንግዲህ ምንድን ነው?
am.B: ታዲያ ምንድን ነው?
am.R: ታዲያ ይህ ምን ማለት ነው?

decisions.choice: What follows from this?
decisions.reason: Paul uses this short question to draw a conclusion from what he has said (3:9, 6:15).

decisions.choice: So what does this mean?
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the short question.

decisions.choice: Que, pois?
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two short words of the Greek; Balanced uses the ordinary Portuguese "E então?" for a question that draws a conclusion.

source.text: ὃ ἐπιζητεῖ Ἰσραήλ, τοῦτο οὐκ ἐπέτυχεν, ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν· οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως, ὀφθαλμοὺς τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τοῦ μὴ ἀκούειν, ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: What is seeking Israel, this not it obtained, but the election obtained [it]; and the rest were hardened, \v 8 as it has been written: Gave to them the God a spirit of stupor, eyes the not to see and ears the not to hear, until the today day.

en.L: What Israel is seeking, this it did not obtain, but the elect obtained [it]; and the rest were hardened, \v 8 just as it is written, "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes [so as] not to see and ears [so as] not to hear, to this very day."
en.B: Israel did not obtain what it was seeking. Those God chose obtained it, but the rest were hardened, \v 8 as it is written, "God has given them a spirit of numbness, eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, to this very day."
en.R: So the people of Israel did not find what they were looking for. Only those God chose found it. God made the rest of them stubborn. \v 8 As Scripture says, "God made their minds dull. He gave them eyes that cannot see and ears that cannot hear, and they are still like that today."

es.L: Lo que Israel busca, eso no lo alcanzó, pero los escogidos [lo] alcanzaron; y los demás fueron endurecidos, \v 8 tal como está escrito: «Dios les dio un espíritu de estupor, ojos para no ver y oídos para no oír, hasta el día de hoy.»
es.B: Israel no alcanzó lo que buscaba. Los que Dios eligió sí lo alcanzaron, pero los demás fueron endurecidos, \v 8 como está escrito: «Dios les ha dado un espíritu de aturdimiento, ojos que no ven y oídos que no oyen, hasta el día de hoy.»
es.R: Así que el pueblo de Israel no encontró lo que buscaba. Solo lo encontraron los que Dios eligió. A los demás, Dios los volvió tercos. \v 8 Como dice la Escritura: «Dios les entorpeció la mente. Les dio ojos que no pueden ver y oídos que no pueden oír, y siguen así hasta hoy.»

sw.L: Kile anachokitafuta Israeli, hicho hakukipata, lakini wateule walikipata; na wale waliobaki walifanywa wagumu, \v 8 kama ilivyoandikwa: "Mungu aliwapa roho ya bumbuazi, macho ya kutoona na masikio ya kutosikia, hadi siku hii ya leo."
sw.B: Israeli hakukipata kile alichokuwa akikitafuta. Wale ambao Mungu aliwachagua walikipata, lakini wengine walifanywa wagumu, \v 8 kama ilivyoandikwa: "Mungu amewapa roho ya bumbuazi, macho yasiyoona na masikio yasiyosikia, hadi leo hii."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watu wa Israeli hawakupata kile walichokuwa wakikitafuta. Ni wale tu ambao Mungu aliwachagua waliokipata. Wengine Mungu aliwafanya wakaidi. \v 8 Kama Maandiko yanavyosema: "Mungu alizifanya akili zao kuwa nzito. Aliwapa macho yasiyoweza kuona na masikio yasiyoweza kusikia, na mpaka leo bado wako hivyo."

fr.L: Ce qu’Israël recherche, il ne l’a pas obtenu, mais les élus [l’]ont obtenu ; et les autres ont été endurcis, \v 8 selon qu’il est écrit : « Dieu leur a donné un esprit de torpeur, des yeux pour ne pas voir et des oreilles pour ne pas entendre, jusqu’à ce jour même. »
fr.B: Israël n’a pas obtenu ce qu’il recherchait. Ceux que Dieu a choisis l’ont obtenu, mais les autres ont été endurcis, \v 8 comme il est écrit : « Dieu leur a donné un esprit d’engourdissement, des yeux qui ne voient pas et des oreilles qui n’entendent pas, jusqu’à ce jour. »
fr.R: Le peuple d’Israël n’a donc pas trouvé ce qu’il cherchait. Seuls ceux que Dieu a choisis l’ont trouvé. Dieu a rendu les autres obstinés. \v 8 Comme le dit l’Écriture : « Dieu a engourdi leur esprit. Il leur a donné des yeux qui ne peuvent pas voir et des oreilles qui ne peuvent pas entendre, et ils sont encore comme cela aujourd’hui. »

ko.L: 이스라엘은 자기가 찾고 있는 것, 이것을 얻지 못하였고, 택하심을 받은 사람들이 [그것을] 얻었습니다. 그리고 나머지 사람들은 완고해졌습니다. \v 8 기록된 대로입니다. "하나님께서 그들에게 혼미한 영을, 보지 못하는 눈과 듣지 못하는 귀를 주셨다. 오늘 이날까지 [그러하다]."
ko.B: 이스라엘은 자기가 찾던 것을 얻지 못했습니다. 하나님께서 택하신 사람들은 그것을 얻었지만, 나머지 사람들은 완고해졌습니다. \v 8 기록된 대로입니다. "하나님께서 그들에게 무감각한 영을 주셨다. 그들은 눈이 있어도 보지 못하고 귀가 있어도 듣지 못한다. 오늘 이날까지 그렇다."
ko.R: 그래서 이스라엘 백성은 그들이 찾던 것을 얻지 못했습니다. 하나님께서 택하신 사람들만 그것을 얻었습니다. 하나님께서는 나머지 사람들을 고집스럽게 만드셨습니다. \v 8 성경에 이렇게 기록되어 있습니다. "하나님께서 그들의 마음을 둔하게 하셨다. 그분은 그들에게 보지 못하는 눈과 듣지 못하는 귀를 주셨다. 그들은 오늘까지도 그렇다."

vi.L: Điều Y-sơ-ra-ên đang tìm kiếm, thì [Y-sơ-ra-ên] đã không đạt được, nhưng những người được chọn đã đạt được; còn những người khác thì đã bị làm cho chai lì, \v 8 như có chép: "Đức Chúa Trời đã ban cho họ một tâm thần mê muội, mắt để không thấy và tai để không nghe, cho đến ngày nay."
vi.B: Y-sơ-ra-ên đã không đạt được điều mình tìm kiếm. Những người được Đức Chúa Trời chọn thì đã đạt được, còn những người khác thì bị làm cho chai lì, \v 8 như có lời chép: "Đức Chúa Trời đã cho họ một tâm thần tê dại, mắt không thấy được và tai không nghe được, cho đến tận ngày nay."
vi.R: Vậy dân Y-sơ-ra-ên đã không tìm được điều họ tìm kiếm. Chỉ những người Đức Chúa Trời chọn mới tìm được. Đức Chúa Trời đã làm cho những người còn lại trở nên ương ngạnh. \v 8 Như Kinh Thánh chép: "Đức Chúa Trời đã làm cho tâm trí họ đờ đẫn. Ngài cho họ mắt mà không thấy, tai mà không nghe, và cho đến ngày nay họ vẫn như thế."

pt.L: O que Israel procura, isso não alcançou, mas os eleitos [o] alcançaram; e os demais foram endurecidos, \v 8 assim como está escrito: "Deus lhes deu um espírito de torpor, olhos para não ver e ouvidos para não ouvir, até o dia de hoje."
pt.B: Israel não alcançou o que procurava. Os que Deus escolheu o alcançaram, mas os demais foram endurecidos, \v 8 como está escrito: "Deus lhes deu um espírito de entorpecimento, olhos que não veem e ouvidos que não ouvem, até o dia de hoje."
pt.R: Por isso o povo de Israel não encontrou o que estava procurando. Só os que Deus escolheu encontraram. Deus deixou os outros teimosos. \v 8 Como diz a Escritura: "Deus deixou a mente deles entorpecida. Deu a eles olhos que não conseguem ver e ouvidos que não conseguem ouvir, e eles continuam assim até hoje."

am.L: እስራኤል የሚፈልገውን ይህን አላገኘም፤ የተመረጡት ግን አገኙት፤ የቀሩትም ደነደኑ፤ \v 8 እንዲህ ተብሎ እንደ ተጻፈ፦ «እግዚአብሔር የድንዛዜ መንፈስን፣ እንዳያዩ ዓይኖችን፣ እንዳይሰሙም ጆሮዎችን እስከ ዛሬ ቀን ድረስ ሰጣቸው።»
am.B: እስራኤል ሲፈልገው የነበረውን አላገኘም። እግዚአብሔር የመረጣቸው ግን አገኙት፤ የቀሩት ግን ደነደኑ፤ \v 8 እንዲህ ተብሎ እንደ ተጻፈ፦ «እግዚአብሔር የመደንዘዝ መንፈስን፣ የማያዩ ዓይኖችንና የማይሰሙ ጆሮዎችን እስከ ዛሬ ድረስ ሰጥቷቸዋል።»
am.R: ስለዚህ የእስራኤል ሕዝብ የሚፈልጉትን አላገኙም። ያገኙት እግዚአብሔር የመረጣቸው ብቻ ናቸው። የቀሩትን ግን እግዚአብሔር ልበ ደንዳና አደረጋቸው። \v 8 መጽሐፍ ቅዱስ እንደሚለው፣ «እግዚአብሔር አእምሮአቸውን አደነዘዘው። ማየት የማይችሉ ዓይኖችንና መስማት የማይችሉ ጆሮዎችን ሰጣቸው፤ እስከ ዛሬም እንደዚያው ናቸው።»

decisions.choice: what Israel seeks: righteousness, being right with God
decisions.reason: Paul has just said that Israel pursued righteousness but did not reach it (9:31, 10:3).

decisions.choice: the elect: those whom God chose
decisions.reason: The noun means "choice" or "election", but here it stands for the people chosen, the remnant of verse 5.

decisions.choice: were hardened: God made them unresponsive
decisions.reason: The passive verb does not name who hardened them, but the quotation that follows says God gave them a spirit of stupor, as in 9:18. Hardening is a picture of becoming unable to see or respond.

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 29:4 with Isaiah 29:10
decisions.reason: Paul joins Moses' words, "the LORD has not given you a heart to know, or eyes to see, or ears to hear, to this day" (Deuteronomy 29:4, 29:3 in Hebrew), with Isaiah 29:10, "the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep". The Hebrew of both has the divine name; Paul writes "God".

decisions.choice: a spirit of stupor: a numbness that keeps them from understanding
decisions.reason: The old Greek translation of Isaiah 29:10 uses this phrase for the Hebrew "spirit of deep sleep". The word means a dazed numbness.

decisions.choice: those God chose
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people meant.

decisions.choice: God made the rest of them stubborn
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who hardened them, as the meaning decision explains, and uses "stubborn" for the picture of hardening.

decisions.choice: As it is written (B); As Scripture says (R)
alternatives: just as it has been written
decisions.reason: "It is written" is the normal formula for quoting Scripture; Readable names Scripture, as in 1:17.

decisions.choice: Israeli with singular personal agreement ("hakukipata")
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks of Israel as one, so Literal and Balanced keep the name singular and give it personal agreement, as a people named like a person. Readable says "watu wa Israeli" with plural agreement, as the English Readable does. A reviewer may prefer plural agreement at every level.

decisions.choice: roho ya bumbuazi
decisions.reason: "Bumbuazi" is a dazed, stunned state, the numbness the meaning decision describes. "Usingizi mzito" (deep sleep) is the Hebrew of Isaiah, not the Greek word Paul uses. Readable says that God made their minds heavy ("akili zao kuwa nzito").

decisions.choice: "완고해지다" (L, B); "고집스럽게 만들다" (R), as for the related verb at 9:18; "완고함" for the noun in verse 25
decisions.reason: The meaning decision says God made them unresponsive; Readable names God as the one who acts, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "혼미한 영" (L); "무감각한 영" (B); "마음을 둔하게 하다" (R)
decisions.reason: A spirit of stupor is a numbness that keeps them from understanding (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "bị làm cho chai lì" (L, B); "ương ngạnh" (R) (also "sự chai lì" in 11:25)
decisions.reason: The verb is to make callous, unresponsive (m3). "Làm cứng lòng" is kept for the different verb of 9:18, so Vietnamese says "chai lì" (grown callous) here; Readable says "ương ngạnh" (stubborn), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "tâm thần mê muội" (L); "tâm thần tê dại" (B), lowercase
decisions.reason: A spirit of stupor is a numbness that keeps them from understanding (m5), not a spirit being, so Vietnamese says "tâm thần", a state of mind, in lower case, as "tinh thần nô lệ" in 8:15.

decisions.choice: os eleitos
decisions.reason: The Greek noun means "election", but it stands for the people chosen (meaning decision); Literal says "os eleitos", as the English Literal says "the elect", because "a eleição" would read as a vote.

decisions.choice: ደነደኑ (were hardened, L, B); ልበ ደንዳና አደረጋቸው (made them stubborn, R)
decisions.reason: The verb means made hard and unresponsive (meaning note m3). The same root gives the noun in 11:25 (መደንደን, ደንድኗል).

decisions.choice: የተመረጡት (those chosen)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the abstract noun for the chosen people themselves; Amharic says who they are, as the English Literal does.

source.text: καὶ Δαυὶδ λέγει· Γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα αὐτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς θήραν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδομα αὐτοῖς, σκοτισθήτωσαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν, καὶ τὸν νῶτον αὐτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον.

records.literal_gloss: And David says: Let become the table of them for a snare and for a trap and for a stumbling block and for a retribution to them, \v 10 let be darkened the eyes of them the not to see, and the back of them through all bend down.

en.L: And David says, "Let their table become a snare and a trap and a stumbling block and a retribution to them; \v 10 let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their back continually."
en.B: And David says, "May their table turn into a snare and a net, a stumbling block and a just penalty for them. \v 10 May their eyes grow dark so that they cannot see, and keep their backs bent forever."
en.R: And David says, "May the meals they enjoy become a trap that catches them. May they trip and fall and get what they deserve. \v 10 May their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see. Keep their backs bent low forever."

es.L: Y David dice: «Conviértase su mesa en lazo y en trampa y en tropiezo y en retribución para ellos; \v 10 oscurézcanse sus ojos para no ver, y encorva su espalda continuamente.»
es.B: Y David dice: «Que su mesa se vuelva para ellos lazo y red, tropiezo y justo castigo. \v 10 Que se les oscurezcan los ojos para que no puedan ver, y haz que su espalda se encorve para siempre.»
es.R: Y David dice: «Que las comidas que disfrutan se conviertan en una trampa que los atrape. Que tropiecen y caigan y reciban lo que merecen. \v 10 Que se les nublen los ojos para que no puedan ver. Haz que anden siempre encorvados.»

sw.L: Na Daudi anasema: "Meza yao igeuke kuwa mtego na kitanzi na kizuizi cha kujikwaa na malipizi juu yao; \v 10 macho yao yafunikwe na giza yasione, na mgongo wao uupinde daima."
sw.B: Na Daudi anasema: "Meza yao na igeuke kuwa mtego na wavu, kikwazo na adhabu wanayostahili. \v 10 Macho yao na yafunikwe na giza wasiweze kuona, na migongo yao uipinde milele."
sw.R: Na Daudi anasema: "Vyakula wanavyovifurahia na viwe mtego wa kuwanasa. Na wajikwae na kuanguka, na wapate kile wanachostahili. \v 10 Macho yao na yafunikwe na giza ili wasiweze kuona. Uwafanye watembee wakiwa wameinama milele."

fr.L: Et David dit : « Que leur table devienne un filet, et un piège, et une occasion de chute, et une rétribution pour eux ; \v 10 que leurs yeux soient obscurcis pour ne pas voir, et courbe continuellement leur dos. »
fr.B: Et David dit : « Que leur table se change en filet et en piège, en occasion de chute et en juste châtiment pour eux. \v 10 Que leurs yeux s’obscurcissent pour qu’ils ne voient plus, et tiens leur dos courbé pour toujours. »
fr.R: Et David dit : « Que les repas dont ils profitent deviennent un piège qui les attrape. Qu’ils trébuchent, qu’ils tombent et qu’ils reçoivent ce qu’ils méritent. \v 10 Que leurs yeux soient obscurcis pour qu’ils ne puissent pas voir. Fais-leur courber le dos pour toujours. »

ko.L: 또 다윗이 말합니다. "그들의 밥상이 그들에게 올무와 덫과 걸림돌과 보응이 되게 하십시오. \v 10 그들의 눈이 어두워져 보지 못하게 하시고, 그들의 등을 언제나 굽게 하십시오."
ko.B: 다윗도 이렇게 말합니다. "그들의 밥상이 그들에게 올무와 그물이 되고, 걸려 넘어지게 하는 돌과 마땅한 벌이 되게 하십시오. \v 10 그들의 눈이 어두워져 보지 못하게 하시고, 그들의 등이 영원히 굽어 있게 하십시오."
ko.R: 다윗도 이렇게 말합니다. "그들이 즐기는 음식이 그들을 잡는 덫이 되게 하십시오. 그들이 걸려 넘어져서 받아 마땅한 벌을 받게 하십시오. \v 10 그들의 눈이 어두워져서 보지 못하게 하십시오. 그들의 등이 영원히 굽어 있게 하십시오."

vi.L: Và Đa-vít nói: "Nguyện bàn ăn của họ trở thành cái bẫy, cái lưới, vật gây vấp ngã và sự báo trả cho họ; \v 10 nguyện mắt họ bị làm cho tối tăm để không thấy, và xin làm cho lưng họ cong xuống luôn luôn."
vi.B: Đa-vít cũng nói: "Nguyện bàn tiệc của họ trở nên cạm bẫy và lưới bắt, thành cớ vấp ngã và hình phạt xứng đáng cho họ. \v 10 Nguyện mắt họ tối lại để không thấy được, và xin khiến lưng họ còng xuống mãi mãi."
vi.R: Đa-vít cũng nói: "Nguyện những bữa tiệc họ vui hưởng trở thành cái bẫy bắt lấy họ. Nguyện họ vấp ngã và nhận lấy điều họ đáng phải chịu. \v 10 Nguyện mắt họ bị tối lại để không thấy được. Xin khiến lưng họ còng xuống mãi mãi."

pt.L: E Davi diz: "Torne-se a mesa deles laço, e armadilha, e tropeço, e retribuição para eles; \v 10 escureçam-se os olhos deles para não verem, e curva as costas deles continuamente."
pt.B: E Davi diz: "Que a mesa deles se torne um laço e uma rede, um tropeço e um justo castigo para eles. \v 10 Que os olhos deles escureçam para não verem, e conserva as costas deles sempre curvadas."
pt.R: E Davi diz: "Que as refeições de que eles gostam se tornem uma armadilha que os prenda. Que eles tropecem, caiam e recebam o que merecem. \v 10 Que os olhos deles fiquem escuros para não verem. Deixa as costas deles sempre curvadas."

am.L: ዳዊትም እንዲህ ይላል፦ «ማዕዳቸው ወጥመድና አሽክላ፣ ማሰናከያና ብድራት ይሁንባቸው፤ \v 10 እንዳያዩ ዓይኖቻቸው ይጨልሙ፤ ጀርባቸውንም ዘወትር አጉብጥ።»
am.B: ዳዊትም እንዲህ ይላል፦ «ማዕዳቸው ወጥመድና መረብ፣ መሰናክልና ተገቢ ቅጣት ይሁንባቸው። \v 10 ማየት እንዳይችሉ ዓይኖቻቸው ይጨልሙ፤ ጀርባቸውንም ለዘላለም አጉብጠው።»
am.R: ዳዊትም እንዲህ ይላል፦ «የሚደሰቱበት ምግባቸው የሚይዛቸው ወጥመድ ይሁን። ተሰናክለው ይውደቁ፤ የሚገባቸውንም ያግኙ። \v 10 ማየት እንዳይችሉ ዓይኖቻቸው ይጨልሙ። ጀርባቸውንም ለዘላለም አጉብጠው።»

decisions.reason: Paul quotes Psalm 69:23-24 (68:23-24 in the old Greek translation) closely, from a psalm headed "Of David". The words "and a trap" are not in that psalm, and the order of the other nouns differs. The psalm is a prayer against those who persecute the righteous sufferer; the New Testament reads it of Jesus (John 2:17, 15:25; Romans 15:3).

decisions.choice: their table: the meals and good things they enjoy and rely on
alternatives: the law and its privileges, which became a trap for them
decisions.reason: In the psalm the table is the enemies' food and feasting, which is to turn against them. Paul does not say what the table stands for in Israel's case; the plain sense is the good things they enjoy becoming the means of their fall.

decisions.choice: a retribution: a fitting repayment
decisions.reason: The noun means a repayment, here a punishment that matches what was done.

decisions.choice: bend their back: bring them under a heavy load
alternatives: bowed down in grief or weakness
decisions.reason: A bent back is the posture of a slave or a person carrying a burden; it can also picture grief. The words continue the picture of darkened eyes: people weighed down and unable to look up.

decisions.choice: continually: for all time
decisions.reason: The phrase means "through everything", that is, all the time.

decisions.choice: May ...
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the Greek third-person commands as wishes, the usual English for a prayer of this kind.

decisions.choice: the meals they enjoy ... a trap ... trip and fall ... get what they deserve
alternatives: their table ... a snare and a trap ... a stumbling block ... a retribution
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the table and gives the four nouns in plain words.

decisions.choice: the psalm's wishes as requests to God in 합쇼체 ("되게 하십시오", "굽게 하십시오")
decisions.reason: The psalm is a prayer, and the command "bend their back" is spoken to God, so the wishes take the 합쇼체 used for words addressed to God (10:16, 11:3). "-소서" is the older prayer ending and is avoided as archaic.

decisions.choice: "밥상" (L, B); "즐기는 음식" (R)
decisions.reason: Their table means the meals and good things they enjoy and rely on (meaning decision); "밥상" is the everyday Korean picture of a meal.

decisions.choice: "Nguyện" for the wishes; "xin" for the command addressed to God
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks wishes in the third person and then a command to God (bend their back). Vietnamese says the wishes with "nguyện" and the request to God with "xin"; "hãy" would sound like an order given to God.

decisions.choice: "bàn ăn" (L); "bàn tiệc" (B); "những bữa tiệc họ vui hưởng" (R)
decisions.reason: Their table is the meals and good things they enjoy and rely on (m2, footnoted). "Bàn" alone could be any piece of furniture, so Literal says "bàn ăn" and Balanced "bàn tiệc", the table of a feast.

decisions.choice: curva (L); conserva (B); Deixa (R): the imperative with "tu"
decisions.reason: The last line is a command to God in the psalm, so it is in the "tu" imperative, the form of prayer at every level; the other wishes are in the third person ("Que ...").

decisions.choice: ማዕድ (table)
decisions.reason: ማዕድ is the meal table and the meal on it, which is what the meaning note says the table stands for; Readable says "የሚደሰቱበት ምግባቸው".

source.text: Λέγω οὖν, μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσιν;

records.literal_gloss: I say then, not they stumbled that they might fall?

en.L: I say then, did they stumble so that they might fall?
en.B: So I ask: did they stumble so as to fall for good?
en.R: So I ask this: When the people of Israel stumbled, did they fall and never get up again?

es.R: Entonces pregunto: Cuando el pueblo de Israel tropezó, ¿cayó para no levantarse más?

sw.L: Basi nasema, je, walijikwaa ili waanguke?

sw.R: Kwa hiyo nauliza hivi: Watu wa Israeli walipojikwaa, je, walianguka wasiinuke tena?

fr.L: Je dis donc : ont-ils trébuché pour tomber ?
fr.B: Je demande donc : auraient-ils trébuché au point de tomber pour de bon ?
fr.R: Alors je pose cette question : quand le peuple d’Israël a trébuché, est-il tombé pour ne plus jamais se relever ?

ko.L: 그러면 내가 말합니다. 그들이 걸려 비틀거린 것이 쓰러지기 위함이었습니까?

ko.R: 그러면 이렇게 묻겠습니다. 이스라엘 백성은 걸려 넘어졌을 때, 아주 쓰러져서 다시 일어나지 못하게 되었습니까?

vi.L: Vậy tôi nói: chẳng lẽ họ đã vấp để rồi ngã [luôn] sao?

vi.R: Vậy tôi hỏi điều này: khi dân Y-sơ-ra-ên vấp ngã, có phải họ đã ngã luôn và không bao giờ đứng dậy được nữa không?

pt.L: Digo, então: tropeçaram para que caíssem?

pt.R: Então eu pergunto: quando o povo de Israel tropeçou, caiu para nunca mais se levantar?

am.L: እንግዲህ እላለሁ፣ እንዲወድቁ ተሰናከሉን?
am.B: እንግዲህ እጠይቃለሁ፤ ተሰናክለው ለዘለቄታው ወደቁን?
am.R: ስለዚህ ይህን እጠይቃለሁ፤ የእስራኤል ሕዝብ በተሰናከሉ ጊዜ ዳግመኛ እንዳይነሡ ሆነው ወደቁን?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, the negative particle expects a denial, which follows at once.

decisions.choice: stumble ... fall: trip up, or fall down for good
alternatives: two words for the same thing
decisions.reason: The contrast between the two verbs carries the point: Israel has stumbled (9:32-33), but has it fallen beyond recovery? The answer is no.

decisions.choice: so as to: with the result that
alternatives: in order that: was their fall God's purpose?
decisions.reason: The conjunction can express purpose or result. Paul's answer, which speaks of what their stumbling led to, fits either; "so as to" keeps both open.

decisions.choice: fall for good (B); fall and never get up again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the contrast with "stumble", which the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

decisions.choice: "걸려 비틀거리다 ... 쓰러지다" (L, B); "걸려 넘어지다 ... 다시 일어나지 못하다" (R)
decisions.reason: The two verbs are a trip and a fall for good (meaning decision); Korean uses two different verbs so the contrast stays.

decisions.choice: "vấp" / "ngã [luôn]" (L); "vấp chân" / "ngã quỵ luôn" (B)
decisions.reason: Paul sets tripping against falling down for good (m2). Vietnamese "vấp ngã" would join the two, so the verbs are kept apart, and "luôn" (for good) says what the second one means, as the English Balanced does.

source.text: μὴ γένοιτο· ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Not may it be; but by the of them trespass the salvation to the Gentiles, for the to provoke to jealousy them.

en.L: May it not be! But by their trespass salvation [has come] to the Gentiles, so as to make them jealous.
en.B: Certainly not! Rather, through their wrongdoing salvation has come to the Gentiles, so that Israel would become jealous.
en.R: Of course not! Because they did wrong, salvation has come to people who are not Jews. That was meant to make the people of Israel jealous.

es.L: ¡No sea así! Sino que por su transgresión [vino] la salvación a los gentiles, para provocarlos a celos.
es.B: ¡De ningún modo! Al contrario, por medio de su transgresión la salvación ha alcanzado a los gentiles, con el fin de despertar los celos de Israel.
es.R: ¡Claro que no! Como ellos hicieron mal, la salvación ha llegado a los que no son judíos. Eso debía hacer que el pueblo de Israel sintiera celos.

sw.L: Isiwe hivyo! Bali kwa kosa lao wokovu [umewafikia] watu wa mataifa, ili kuwatia wivu.
sw.B: Hasha! Badala yake, kupitia kosa lao wokovu umewafikia watu wa mataifa, ili kuwafanya Waisraeli waone wivu.
sw.R: Sivyo kabisa! Kwa sababu walikosea, wokovu umewafikia watu wasio Wayahudi. Jambo hilo lilikusudiwa kuwafanya watu wa Israeli waone wivu.

fr.L: Qu’il n’en soit rien ! Mais par leur faux pas, le salut [est venu] aux nations, pour les rendre jaloux.
fr.B: Absolument pas ! Au contraire, par leur faute, le salut est venu aux non-Juifs, pour qu’Israël devienne jaloux.
fr.R: Pas du tout ! Parce qu’ils ont mal agi, le salut est arrivé à ceux qui ne sont pas juifs. Cela devait rendre le peuple d’Israël jaloux.

ko.L: 결코 그럴 수 없습니다! 오히려 그들의 범죄로 구원이 이방 사람들에게 [이르렀으니], 이는 그들을 시기하게 하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 절대로 그렇지 않습니다! 오히려 그들의 범죄 때문에 구원이 이방 사람들에게 이르렀고, 그것은 이스라엘이 시기하게 하려는 것이었습니다.
ko.R: 절대 아닙니다! 그들이 잘못했기 때문에, 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 구원이 왔습니다. 그것은 이스라엘 백성이 질투하게 하려는 것이었습니다.

vi.L: Không hề như vậy! Nhưng bởi sự vi phạm của họ, sự cứu rỗi [đã đến] cho các dân ngoại, để khiến họ ganh tị.
vi.B: Chẳng hề như vậy! Trái lại, qua sự vi phạm của họ, các dân ngoại đã được cứu, để Y-sơ-ra-ên phải ganh tị.
vi.R: Không đời nào! Vì họ đã làm sai, những người không phải Do Thái đã được cứu. Điều đó là để làm cho dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ganh tị.

pt.L: Que não aconteça! Mas, pela transgressão deles, a salvação [veio] às nações, para provocá-los a ciúmes.
pt.B: De forma alguma! Pelo contrário, por causa do erro deles a salvação chegou aos não judeus, para que Israel ficasse com ciúmes.
pt.R: Claro que não! Porque eles erraram, a salvação chegou aos que não são judeus. Isso devia deixar o povo de Israel com ciúmes.

am.L: ከቶ አይሁን! ነገር ግን በበደላቸው መዳን ለአሕዛብ [መጣ]፤ [ይህም] እነርሱን ለማስቀናት [ነው]።
am.B: በፍጹም! ይልቁንም እስራኤል እንዲቀና በበደላቸው ምክንያት መዳን ወደ አሕዛብ መጥቷል።
am.R: በጭራሽ! ስሕተት በመሥራታቸው ምክንያት መዳን አይሁድ ወዳልሆኑ ሕዝቦች መጣ። ይህም የእስራኤልን ሕዝብ ለማስቀናት ነበር።

decisions.choice: the strongest possible denial
decisions.reason: μὴ γένοιτο, "may it not happen", is Paul's strongest way of rejecting a false conclusion (3:4, 6:2, 9:14; Galatians 2:17).

decisions.choice: trespass: a false step, a wrong
decisions.reason: The noun means a false step, continuing the picture of stumbling. Here it is Israel's refusal to believe in the Messiah (10:16-21).

decisions.choice: Deuteronomy 32:21
decisions.reason: Paul has just quoted God's words, "I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation" (10:19). Salvation coming to the Gentiles is meant to stir Israel to want it too.

decisions.choice: by their trespass: their trespass was the occasion for salvation to go out
decisions.reason: When Jews rejected the gospel, the apostles turned to the Gentiles (Acts 13:46, 28:28). Paul does not say Israel's sin saves anyone, but that God used it.

decisions.choice: Certainly not! (B); Of course not! (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use ordinary English for an emphatic no. "God forbid" adds a word for God that the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing (B); they did wrong (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the wrong step.

decisions.choice: Israel (B); the people of Israel (R)
decisions.reason: English "them" could seem to mean the Gentiles; Balanced and Readable name Israel.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Gentiles" means, as in 1:16.

decisions.choice: transgresión
decisions.reason: "Transgresión" is the settled word for this noun in Paul (Colossians 2:13) and keeps the picture of a false step. Readable says "hicieron mal", as the English Readable says "did wrong". The same applies in verse 12.

decisions.choice: kosa
decisions.reason: "Kosa" (a fault, a wrong step) is the word used for this noun in Colossians 2:13 and Ephesians, and it keeps the picture of stumbling better than "dhambi" (sin). Readable uses the verb "walikosea". The same applies in verse 12.

decisions.choice: les nations (L); les non-Juifs (B); ceux qui ne sont pas juifs (R), as in 9:24 (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "the nations", and Paul uses it for everyone who is not a Jew. Literal keeps "nations". "Les païens", the traditional word, today means people with no faith or with pagan religion, which is not Paul’s point; "Gentils" is not French in this sense. Balanced says "les non-Juifs" and Readable "ceux qui ne sont pas juifs", as the English Readable says "people who are not Jews".

decisions.choice: faux pas (L, and R in 11:12); faute (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a false step, and Literal keeps the picture that follows on from "stumbled" in the question before. "Chute" would blur it with "tomber", the fall that Paul denies. Balanced says "faute", as the English Balanced says "wrongdoing".

decisions.choice: "결코 그럴 수 없습니다!" (L); "절대로 그렇지 않습니다!" (B); "절대 아닙니다!" (R), as settled at 3:4
decisions.reason: The same fixed form for each level as through the letter.

decisions.choice: "범죄" (L, B), as in 5:15-20; "잘못하다" (R); "시기하게 하다" (L, B) / "질투하게 하다" (R), as at 10:19
decisions.reason: The trespass is a false step, a wrong (meaning decision); the same Korean as in chapter 5 at Literal and Balanced. Readable uses the plainer "잘못", which keeps the picture of a misstep better than "죄".

decisions.choice: "sự vi phạm" (L, B); "làm sai" (R) (also 11:12)
decisions.reason: The word is a false step (m2), the word kept as "sự vi phạm" in 4:25 and chapter 5. Here it plays on the stumbling of the question before, which "vi phạm" (a step across the line) keeps.

decisions.choice: as nações (L); os não judeus (B); os que não são judeus (R)
decisions.reason: The terms table: Literal keeps the Greek word "nações", Balanced says "os não judeus" where the English says "Gentiles", and Readable says it as a plain clause, as the English Readable does. "Gentios" is church language many readers do not know.

source.text: εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος κόσμου καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλοῦτος ἐθνῶν, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: If and the trespass of them riches of world and the loss of them riches of Gentiles, how much more the fullness of them.

en.L: Now if their trespass [means] riches for [the] world, and their loss [means] riches for [the] Gentiles, how much more their fullness!
en.B: Now if their wrongdoing means riches for the world, and their loss means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater riches their fullness will bring!
en.R: Their wrong step brought great blessing to the world. Their loss brought great blessing to people who are not Jews. So think how much greater the blessing will be when their full number is brought in!

es.L: Y si su transgresión [es] riqueza para [el] mundo, y su pérdida riqueza para [los] gentiles, ¡cuánto más su plenitud!
es.B: Ahora bien, si su transgresión significa riqueza para el mundo, y su pérdida significa riqueza para los gentiles, ¡cuánta mayor riqueza traerá su plenitud!
es.R: Su paso en falso trajo una gran bendición al mundo. Su pérdida trajo una gran bendición a los que no son judíos. ¡{{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} cuánto mayor será la bendición cuando haya entrado su número completo!

sw.L: Na ikiwa kosa lao [ni] utajiri kwa ulimwengu, na hasara yao utajiri kwa watu wa mataifa, utimilifu wao [utakuwa] zaidi sana kiasi gani!
sw.B: Basi, ikiwa kosa lao limeleta utajiri kwa ulimwengu, na kushindwa kwao kumeleta utajiri kwa watu wa mataifa, utimilifu wao utaleta utajiri mkubwa zaidi kiasi gani!
sw.R: Kosa lao lilileta baraka kubwa kwa ulimwengu. Hasara yao iliwaletea baraka kubwa watu wasio Wayahudi. Basi fikirini jinsi baraka itakavyokuwa kubwa zaidi idadi yao kamili itakapoingia!

fr.L: Or si leur faux pas [est une] richesse pour [le] monde, et leur échec une richesse pour [les] nations, combien plus leur plénitude !
fr.B: Or si leur faute a été une richesse pour le monde, et leur échec une richesse pour les non-Juifs, combien plus grande sera la richesse quand ils seront au complet !
fr.R: Leur faux pas a apporté une grande bénédiction au monde. Leur échec a apporté une grande bénédiction à ceux qui ne sont pas juifs. Alors, pensez combien la bénédiction sera plus grande quand ils seront tous rassemblés !

ko.L: 그런데 그들의 범죄가 세상의 부요함이 되고, 그들의 실패가 이방 사람들의 부요함이 되었다면, 그들의 충만함은 얼마나 더 [그러하겠습니까]!
ko.B: 그들의 범죄가 세상에 부요함을 가져다주고 그들의 실패가 이방 사람들에게 부요함을 가져다주었다면, 그들이 다 채워질 때에는 얼마나 더 큰 부요함을 가져다주겠습니까!
ko.R: 그들의 잘못은 세상에 큰 복을 가져왔습니다. 그들의 실패는 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 큰 복을 가져왔습니다. 그렇다면 그들의 수가 다 채워질 때에는 얼마나 더 큰 복이 오겠습니까!

vi.L: Mà nếu sự vi phạm của họ [là] sự giàu có cho thế gian, và sự thất bại của họ [là] sự giàu có cho các dân ngoại, huống chi sự đầy trọn của họ!
vi.B: Mà nếu sự vi phạm của họ đã đem lại sự giàu có cho thế gian, và sự thất bại của họ đã đem lại sự giàu có cho các dân ngoại, thì sự trọn vẹn của họ sẽ đem lại sự giàu có lớn hơn biết bao!
vi.R: Bước sai của họ đã đem lại phước lớn cho thế gian. Sự thất bại của họ đã đem lại phước lớn cho những người không phải Do Thái. Vậy hãy nghĩ xem phước ấy sẽ còn lớn hơn biết bao khi trọn số dân của họ được đem vào!

pt.L: Ora, se a transgressão deles [significa] riqueza para [o] mundo, e a perda deles, riqueza para [as] nações, quanto mais a plenitude deles!
pt.B: Ora, se o erro deles significa riqueza para o mundo, e a perda deles, riqueza para os não judeus, quanto maior riqueza trará a plenitude deles!
pt.R: O passo errado deles trouxe grande bênção para o mundo. A perda deles trouxe grande bênção para os que não são judeus. Então pensem em como a bênção vai ser muito maior quando o número completo deles for trazido!

am.L: በደላቸው ለዓለም ብልጽግና፣ ኪሳራቸውም ለአሕዛብ ብልጽግና [ከሆነ]፣ ሙላታቸውማ እንዴት አብልጦ [ይሆን]!
am.B: በደላቸው ለዓለም ብልጽግና ከሆነ፣ ኪሳራቸውም ለአሕዛብ ብልጽግና ከሆነ፣ ሙላታቸው ምንኛ የበለጠ ብልጽግና ያመጣ ይሆን!
am.R: ስሕተታቸው ለዓለም ታላቅ በረከት አመጣ። ኪሳራቸውም አይሁድ ላልሆኑ ሕዝቦች ታላቅ በረከት አመጣ። እንግዲያስ ሙሉ ቁጥራቸው ሲገባ በረከቱ ምን ያህል የበለጠ እንደሚሆን አስቡት!

decisions.choice: the world: humanity, the nations beyond Israel
decisions.reason: Parallel to "the Gentiles", the world here is the human race to whom the gospel now goes.

decisions.choice: their loss: their defeat or failure
alternatives: their reduction to a small number, in contrast with their "fullness"
decisions.reason: The noun means a defeat or loss. Set against "fullness", some take it to mean that Israel has been reduced to a remnant.

decisions.choice: their fullness: their full number, Israel restored as a whole
decisions.reason: The same word is used of "the full number of the Gentiles" in verse 25, and verse 26 says that all Israel will be saved. Paul looks forward to the time when Israel as a whole is brought in.

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If Israel's failure has brought such blessing, their restoration will bring far more, as verse 15 says.

decisions.choice: great blessing
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of riches means: spiritual blessing.

decisions.choice: when their full number is brought in
decisions.reason: Readable follows the meaning decision and uses the same wording as verse 25.

decisions.choice: people who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Gentiles" means.

decisions.choice: ¡{{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} cuánto mayor será ...!
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "think how much greater". Spanish puts the invitation to the readers in a plural verb, so it carries a plural_you span.

decisions.choice: leur plénitude (L); quand ils seront au complet (B); quand ils seront tous rassemblés (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as their full number, Israel restored as a whole. "Plénitude" keeps the Greek word, the same as "the fullness of the Gentiles" in 11:25, but it is abstract; Balanced and Readable say the full number in plain words. "Conversion" would say more than the Greek does.

decisions.choice: "충만함" (L); "다 채워질 때" (B); "수가 다 채워질 때" (R)
decisions.reason: Their fullness is their full number, Israel restored as a whole (meaning decision, footnoted). Literal keeps the noun; Balanced and Readable say it with a verb.

decisions.choice: "부요함" (L, B); "큰 복" (R)
decisions.reason: Riches here are spiritual blessing; Readable says "큰 복", as the English Readable says "great blessing".

decisions.choice: "sự đầy trọn" (L); "sự trọn vẹn" (B); "trọn số" (R) (also 11:25)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as their full number, Israel restored as a whole, with a footnote. Literal and Balanced keep a word for fullness that leaves the footnoted sense open; Readable says full number, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "huống chi" (L)
decisions.reason: "Huống chi" is the form kept for this argument from the lesser to the greater (m4) since 5:9.

source.text: Ὑμῖν δὲ λέγω τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.

records.literal_gloss: To you and I speak the Gentiles.

en.L: But I am speaking to you, the Gentiles.
en.B: Now I am speaking to you who are Gentiles.
en.R: Now I am speaking to you who are not Jews.

es.L: Pero a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} hablo, a los gentiles.
es.B: Ahora me dirijo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los gentiles.
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:les|os}} hablo a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que no {{plural_you:son|sois}} judíos.

sw.L: Lakini ninasema nanyi, watu wa mataifa.
sw.B: Sasa ninasema nanyi mlio watu wa mataifa.
sw.R: Sasa ninasema nanyi ambao si Wayahudi.

fr.L: Mais c’est à vous, [gens des] nations, que je parle.
fr.B: Je m’adresse maintenant à vous, les non-Juifs.
fr.R: Maintenant, c’est à vous qui n’êtes pas juifs que je parle.

ko.L: 이제 나는 여러분 이방 사람들에게 말합니다.
ko.B: 이제 나는 이방 사람인 여러분에게 말합니다.
ko.R: 이제 나는 유대인이 아닌 여러분에게 말합니다.

vi.L: Nhưng tôi nói với anh chị em, là các dân ngoại.
vi.B: Bây giờ tôi nói với anh chị em là những người dân ngoại.
vi.R: Bây giờ tôi nói với anh chị em, là những người không phải Do Thái.

pt.L: Mas eu falo a vocês, [que são das] nações.
pt.B: Agora falo a vocês, os não judeus.
pt.R: Agora estou falando a vocês, que não são judeus.

am.L: ለእናንተ ለአሕዛብ ግን እናገራለሁ።
am.B: እንግዲህ የምናገረው አሕዛብ ለሆናችሁ ለእናንተ ነው።
am.R: አሁን የምናገረው አይሁድ ላልሆናችሁ ለእናንተ ነው።

decisions.choice: the Gentile believers in Rome
decisions.reason: Paul turns to the Gentile believers among his readers. The church in Rome had both Jewish and Gentile members (1:13, 16:3-15), and here he warns the Gentiles against looking down on Israel.

decisions.choice: you who are not Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says what "Gentiles" means.

source.text: ἐφ’ ὅσον μὲν οὖν εἰμι ἐγὼ ἐθνῶν ἀπόστολος, τὴν διακονίαν μου δοξάζω, εἴ πως παραζηλώσω μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ σώσω τινὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Inasmuch as indeed then am I of Gentiles apostle, the ministry of me I glorify, \v 14 if somehow I may provoke to jealousy of me the flesh and may save some of them.

en.L: Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of [the] Gentiles, I glorify my ministry, \v 14 if somehow I may make my flesh jealous and save some of them.
en.B: So since I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I make much of my ministry, \v 14 in the hope that somehow I may make my own flesh and blood jealous and save some of them.
en.R: God sent me as an apostle to people who are not Jews, so I make much of this work. \v 14 I hope that in some way I can make my own people, the Jews, jealous, and save some of them.

es.L: Por cuanto, pues, yo soy apóstol de [los] gentiles, glorifico mi ministerio, \v 14 por si de algún modo provoco a celos a mi carne y salvo a algunos de ellos.
es.B: Así que, ya que soy apóstol para los gentiles, doy gran valor a mi ministerio, \v 14 con la esperanza de despertar de algún modo los celos de los de mi propia sangre y salvar a algunos de ellos.
es.R: Dios me envió como apóstol a los que no son judíos, por eso doy mucha importancia a este trabajo. \v 14 Espero que de alguna manera pueda hacer que mi propio pueblo, los judíos, sienta celos, y así salvar a algunos de ellos.

sw.L: Basi kwa kadiri nilivyo mtume wa watu wa mataifa, naitukuza huduma yangu, \v 14 ili kwa njia yoyote niutie wivu mwili wangu na kuwaokoa baadhi yao.
sw.B: Basi, kwa kuwa mimi ni mtume kwa watu wa mataifa, naipa huduma yangu uzito mkubwa, \v 14 nikitumaini kwamba kwa namna fulani nitawatia wivu ndugu zangu wa damu na kuwaokoa baadhi yao.
sw.R: Mungu alinituma kama mtume kwa watu wasio Wayahudi, kwa hiyo naiona kazi hii kuwa ya maana sana. \v 14 Natumaini kwamba kwa namna fulani nitawafanya watu wa taifa langu, Wayahudi, waone wivu, nami niwaokoe baadhi yao.

fr.L: Dans la mesure donc où moi, je suis apôtre des nations, je glorifie mon ministère, \v 14 si par quelque moyen je peux rendre jalouse ma chair et en sauver quelques-uns.
fr.B: Puisque je suis l’apôtre des non-Juifs, je fais grand cas de mon ministère, \v 14 dans l’espoir de rendre jaloux ceux de mon propre sang et d’en sauver quelques-uns.
fr.R: Dieu m’a envoyé comme apôtre auprès de ceux qui ne sont pas juifs, alors j’accorde une grande importance à ce travail. \v 14 J’espère ainsi rendre jaloux les gens de mon peuple, les Juifs, et en sauver quelques-uns.

ko.L: 그러므로 내가 이방 사람들의 사도인 만큼, 나는 내 직분을 영광스럽게 여깁니다. \v 14 어떻게든 내 육신을 시기하게 하여 그들 가운데 몇 사람이라도 구원하려는 것입니다.
ko.B: 내가 이방 사람들을 위한 사도인 만큼, 나는 내 직분을 귀하게 여깁니다. \v 14 그렇게 해서 어떻게든 내 동족이 시기하게 하여, 그들 가운데 몇 사람이라도 구원하고 싶습니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 나를 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 사도로 보내셨습니다. 그래서 나는 이 일을 아주 소중하게 여깁니다. \v 14 나는 어떻게든 내 민족인 유대인들이 질투하게 해서, 그들 가운데 몇 사람이라도 구원하고 싶습니다.

vi.L: Vậy, vì tôi là sứ đồ của các dân ngoại, tôi tôn vinh chức vụ của tôi, \v 14 [mong rằng] bằng cách nào đó tôi có thể khiến [những người cùng] xác thịt với tôi ganh tị và cứu được một số người trong họ.
vi.B: Vì tôi là sứ đồ cho các dân ngoại, tôi rất coi trọng chức vụ của mình, \v 14 mong rằng bằng cách nào đó tôi có thể làm cho đồng bào ruột thịt của tôi ganh tị và cứu được một số người trong họ.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã sai tôi làm sứ đồ cho những người không phải Do Thái, nên tôi rất coi trọng công việc này. \v 14 Tôi mong rằng bằng cách nào đó tôi có thể làm cho chính dân tộc tôi, là người Do Thái, ganh tị, và cứu được một số người trong họ.

pt.L: Enquanto, pois, eu sou apóstolo das nações, glorifico o meu ministério, \v 14 se de algum modo eu provocar a ciúmes a minha carne e salvar alguns deles.
pt.B: Por isso, sendo eu apóstolo dos não judeus, dou grande valor ao meu ministério, \v 14 na esperança de provocar de algum modo ciúmes nos do meu próprio sangue e salvar alguns deles.
pt.R: Deus me enviou como apóstolo aos que não são judeus, por isso dou grande valor a esse trabalho. \v 14 Espero conseguir de algum modo deixar com ciúmes o meu próprio povo, os judeus, e salvar alguns deles.

am.L: እንግዲህ እኔ የአሕዛብ ሐዋርያ እስከ ሆንኩ ድረስ አገልግሎቴን አከብራለሁ፤ \v 14 ምናልባት ሥጋዬን አስቀንቼ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶችን አድን እንደ ሆነ።
am.B: ስለዚህ እኔ ለአሕዛብ ሐዋርያ እንደ መሆኔ መጠን አገልግሎቴን ከፍ አድርጌ እመለከተዋለሁ፤ \v 14 ይህንም የማደርገው በሆነ መንገድ የሥጋ ዘመዶቼን አስቀንቼ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶችን አድን ይሆናል ብዬ ተስፋ በማድረግ ነው።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር አይሁድ ወዳልሆኑ ሕዝቦች ሐዋርያ አድርጎ ልኮኛል፤ ስለዚህ ለዚህ ሥራዬ ትልቅ ዋጋ እሰጣለሁ። \v 14 በሆነ መንገድ የገዛ ሕዝቤን፣ አይሁድን፣ አስቀንቼ ከእነርሱ አንዳንዶችን ለማዳን ተስፋ አደርጋለሁ።

decisions.choice: I glorify: I honor my ministry and make the most of it
alternatives: I praise God for my ministry
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to give glory, but with "my ministry" as its object it means to hold it in honor and give it full weight, in the hope of the result verse 14 names.

decisions.choice: my flesh: my own people, my fellow Jews
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means physical kinship, as in 9:3, "my kindred according to the flesh".

decisions.choice: save some: bring some to salvation through the gospel
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of saving people as the one who brings them the gospel, as in 1 Corinthians 9:22. Elsewhere it is God who saves (11:26).

decisions.choice: make much of
decisions.reason: "Glorify my ministry" sounds odd in English; Balanced and Readable give the sense described in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: my own flesh and blood
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the word "flesh" in a natural English phrase for kin.

decisions.choice: my own people, the Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who are meant.

decisions.choice: God sent me as an apostle to people who are not Jews
alternatives: I am an apostle of the Gentiles
decisions.reason: An apostle is one sent; Readable names God as the sender (1:1, 1:5).

decisions.choice: los de mi propia sangre
decisions.reason: Where the English Balanced keeps "flesh" in "my own flesh and blood", Spanish speaks of relatives as those of one's blood; "mi carne y sangre" is not a usual Spanish way of naming one's people. The sense is the kinship the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: ndugu zangu wa damu
decisions.reason: "Mwili wangu" (my body) cannot mean one's relatives in Swahili, so Balanced says "ndugu zangu wa damu" (my blood relatives), the kinship the meaning decision describes. Literal keeps "mwili".

decisions.choice: "영광스럽게 여기다" (L); "귀하게 여기다" (B); "소중하게 여기다" (R)
decisions.reason: Paul honors his ministry and makes the most of it (meaning decision). "영광을 돌리다" is kept for glorifying God (1:21).

decisions.choice: "내 육신" (L); "내 동족" (B); "내 민족인 유대인들" (R)
decisions.reason: My flesh means my own people, my fellow Jews (meaning decision). Literal keeps the letter's word "육신"; Balanced uses "동족" as at 9:3.

decisions.choice: "tôn vinh" (L); "rất coi trọng" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Paul honors his ministry and makes the most of it (m1). Literal keeps "tôn vinh", the verb set for glorify; Balanced and Readable say "coi trọng", as the English says "make much of".

decisions.choice: "[những người cùng] xác thịt với tôi" (L); "đồng bào ruột thịt của tôi" (B)
decisions.reason: My flesh is my own people, my fellow Jews (m2). Literal keeps "xác thịt", the word for flesh through the letter, and brackets what it means; Balanced uses "đồng bào ruột thịt" of 9:3.

decisions.choice: os do meu próprio sangue
decisions.reason: Portuguese speaks of kin as "sangue" ("os do meu sangue"); "a minha carne" alone would be read as Paul's body. This keeps a picture word, as the English Balanced "flesh and blood" does; Literal keeps "a minha carne".

decisions.choice: ሥጋዬ (my flesh, L); የሥጋ ዘመዶቼ (my kin, B); የገዛ ሕዝቤ, አይሁድ (my own people, the Jews, R)
decisions.reason: Here flesh means Paul's fellow Jews (meaning note m2), not the sinful nature. Literal keeps the word; Balanced uses the common Amharic phrase for blood relatives; Readable names them.

source.text: εἰ γὰρ ἡ ἀποβολὴ αὐτῶν καταλλαγὴ κόσμου, τίς ἡ πρόσλημψις εἰ μὴ ζωὴ ἐκ νεκρῶν;

records.literal_gloss: If for the rejection of them reconciliation of world, what the acceptance if not life from dead?

en.L: For if their rejection [means the] reconciliation of [the] world, what [will their] acceptance [be] but life from [the] dead?
en.B: For if their rejection means the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance mean? Nothing less than life from the dead!
en.R: When God set them aside, the world was brought back to God and made friends with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So what will it be like when God takes them back? It will be life from the dead!

es.L: Porque si su rechazo [es la] reconciliación del mundo, ¿qué [será su] aceptación sino vida de entre [los] muertos?
es.B: Porque si su rechazo significa la reconciliación del mundo, ¿qué significará su aceptación? ¡Nada menos que vida de entre los muertos!
es.R: Cuando Dios los apartó, el mundo pudo volver a Dios y ser {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amigo. Entonces, ¿cómo será cuando Dios los reciba de nuevo? ¡Será vida de entre los muertos!

sw.L: Kwa maana ikiwa kukataliwa kwao [ni] upatanisho wa ulimwengu, kupokelewa kwao [kutakuwa] nini, isipokuwa uzima kutoka kwa wafu?
sw.B: Kwa maana ikiwa kukataliwa kwao kunaleta upatanisho wa ulimwengu, kupokelewa kwao kutaleta nini? Si kitu kingine ila uzima kutoka kwa wafu!
sw.R: Mungu alipowaweka kando, ulimwengu ulirudishwa kwa Mungu na kuwa rafiki {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Basi itakuwaje Mungu atakapowapokea tena? Itakuwa uzima kutoka kwa wafu!

fr.L: Car si leur rejet [est la] réconciliation du monde, que [sera leur] accueil, sinon une vie d’entre [les] morts ?
fr.B: Car si leur rejet a été la réconciliation du monde, que sera leur accueil ? Rien de moins que la vie d’entre les morts !
fr.R: Quand Dieu les a mis de côté, le monde a été ramené à Dieu et a fait la paix avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Alors, que se passera-t-il quand Dieu les reprendra ? Ce sera la vie qui sort de la mort !

ko.L: 그들을 버리심이 세상의 화해가 된다면, 그들을 받아들이심은 죽은 사람들 가운데서 [나는] 생명이 아니면 무엇이겠습니까?
ko.B: 하나님께서 그들을 버리신 것이 세상과 하나님의 화해를 가져왔다면, 그들을 받아들이시는 것은 무엇을 가져오겠습니까? 그것은 바로 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나는 생명입니다!
ko.R: 하나님께서 그들을 한쪽으로 제쳐 두셨을 때, 세상 사람들이 하나님께 돌아와 하나님의 친구가 되었습니다. 그렇다면 하나님께서 그들을 다시 받아들이실 때에는 어떻겠습니까? 그것은 죽은 사람들이 다시 살아나는 것과 같은 일일 것입니다!

vi.L: Vì nếu việc họ bị loại bỏ [là] sự hòa giải cho thế gian, thì việc [họ được] tiếp nhận [sẽ là] gì, nếu không phải là sự sống từ kẻ chết?
vi.B: Vì nếu việc họ bị gạt sang một bên đã đem thế gian đến chỗ được hòa giải, thì việc họ được tiếp nhận sẽ là gì? Không gì khác hơn là sự sống từ cõi chết!
vi.R: Khi Đức Chúa Trời gạt họ sang một bên, thế gian được đem trở về với Đức Chúa Trời và trở nên bạn hữu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vậy khi Đức Chúa Trời nhận họ trở lại thì sẽ ra sao? Đó sẽ là sự sống từ cõi chết!

pt.L: Pois, se a rejeição deles [significa a] reconciliação do mundo, que [será a] aceitação [deles], senão vida dentre [os] mortos?
